cannibalisation_check.verdict: No cannibalisation. No page of ours targets 'honeymoon planner' or explains the service. The packages page sells; this explains and hands over to it. Write the article.

cross_market_insights: The SERP is fractured and weak. Sydney and Brisbane top 3 are a parked exact-match domain, an off-intent destination piece and an empty holding page. Melbourne shows agency homepages (one AU, one US) and The Knot's DIY spreadsheet. No result explains what a honeymoon planner is or does.

Intent is split three ways: a service (agencies, specialists), a DIY tool (related searches: template, book, app, free, printable PDF) and general 'how to plan a honeymoon'. A clear service explainer that names the difference in its first lines can win the service intent.

PAA is about money: 'How much do honeymoon planners cost?', 'Is $5000 / $3,000 enough?', 'realistic budget', 'how much does a travel agent make on a $10,000 trip?'. Nobody ranking answers cost or worth it honestly for a luxury traveller.

The Reddit thread (exhausted planning a honeymoon on top of a wedding, has anyone used an agent?) is the real reader question and only social answers it. Our edge: one team across wedding and honeymoon.
No volume data for any variant (API gap), so prioritise by SERP weakness: page one is beatable with one substantive Australian page.
payload.recommended_angle: Answer the confusion first: a honeymoon planner here means a specialist who designs and books the trip, not a printable notebook. Then show what the service actually covers from first call to coming home (including the invisible work: handover from the wedding, transfers between stays, inclusions confirmed in writing, someone reachable while away), compare it honestly with booking direct and with a general travel agent, say when it is worth it and when it is not, and give a short selection checklist. Close with how Wedded Wonderland plans honeymoons as one journey with the wedding.
